comments.content: This stops preserving write-set order for increments. For example, committing two increments of the same meta record queues both `get`s before either callback queues its `put`; both read N and write N+1, so the commit succeeds but loses one increment. A subsequent put/delete of that record can likewise be overwritten by the delayed put. Preserve sequential execution for dependent writes while still routing request failures through the transaction error mapping (and add a same-record, two-increment regression test).

Errors thrown inside this callback no longer propagate to `commit`. For example, if the increment target is missing, indexing `record` throws a TypeError, which the existing `request.catch` silently consumes. No IndexedDB request fails in that case, so `tx.done` resolves and the method returns `Committed` with the other writes persisted but no increment. Ensure callback failures abort the transaction and propagate to the caller, rather than relying exclusively on `tx.done` to detect them.
